preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for x in [n]) and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in [l]) and all(0 <= int(x) <= 10**9 for x in [w])
preconditions.description: Input constraints: n is the number of vertices (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5), l is the maximum path length (1 ≤ l ≤ n), and w is the maximum path weight (0 ≤ w ≤ 10^9).

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= int(p) < (i + 2) <= n for i, (p, _) in enumerate(edges)) and all(0 <= int(w) <= 10**4 for _, w in edges)
preconditions.description: The tree has exactly n-1 edges, each connecting vertex (i+1) to parent p_i (1 ≤ p_i < i+1), with non-negative weights (0 ≤ w_i ≤ 10^4).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in set().union(*[set([int(p), i+2]) for i, (p, _) in enumerate(edges)]))
preconditions.description: All vertices are uniquely indexed from 1 to n, and edges connect valid pairs of vertices.

postconditions.description: Output is a non-negative integer representing the count of close vertex pairs (v, u) where v < u, and the count does not exceed the total possible pairs (n choose 2).

postconditions.expression: all(v < u and (path_length(v, u) <= l and path_weight(v, u) <= w) for v, u in close_pairs) and len(close_pairs) == int(stdout.strip())
postconditions.description: The output count matches the number of vertex pairs (v, u) with v < u where the path length between v and u is at most l and the path weight is at most w. Here, path_length(v, u) is the number of edges in the unique path between v and u, and path_weight(v, u) is the sum of edge weights along that path.
